selection: The same 33 SHA-256-pinned, unchanged AndroidBible production sources as the prior survey. Each target was compiled separately.

features.name: Trailing lambda arguments after omitted defaults
features.scope: Outside-parentheses trailing lambdas mapped to the last parameter after omitted defaults and named arguments; ordinary source and compiled generic, nullable function, member, extension and overload resolution, labels, inline returns and evaluation order
restrictions: Existing bounded language and interop restrictions still apply
General nonfinal vararg parameters remain outside this slice
No full Android module/application or performance claim

features.name: Stable property-path smartcasts in friend dependencies
features.scope: Compiled Kotlin final default val property smartcasts after null guards, with stable immutable local receiver identity and chains, constrained to explicit friend dependencies
restrictions: Source property headers do not yet expose stability
Mutable local receivers and captured receivers remain unsupported
No open, delegated, custom getter, mutable property, extension property or ordinary external module smartcasts
No application build or performance claim

features.name: Implicit and nested classifier type references
features.scope: Implicit same-package/default classifier lookup in body type syntax and direct nested Java/Kotlin classifier lookup through declared member metadata, including generic Java nested type signatures.
restrictions: Inherited Java member-class lookup and protected Java nested classifiers remain unsupported.
No Android, app-build or performance claim; independent fixtures use actual javac and pinned Kotlin compiler dependencies.

features.name: Java platform bounds for Kotlin type parameters
features.scope: Kotlin type parameters with nullable upper bounds satisfy compatible Java platform upper bounds, while nonnull Kotlin bounds and incompatible Java bounds still reject. Implicit same-package/default classifier lookup in body type syntax and direct nested Java/Kotlin classifier lookup through declared member metadata, including generic Java nested type signatures.
restrictions: Inherited Java member-class lookup and protected Java nested classifiers remain unsupported.
No Android, app-build or performance claim; independent fixtures use actual javac and pinned Kotlin compiler dependencies.

features.name: Passive declaration annotations on imported enum constants
features.scope: Passive declaration annotations with payloads on imported enum constant fields, retaining actual runtime field reads and annotation data
restrictions: Exact public/static/final enum constants with self-typed descriptors only
No recovery for ordinary annotated fields, field signatures, type-use annotations, synthetic fields, nullability/type-qualifier annotations or Kotlin semantic annotations and opt-in meta-annotations
Passive annotation inspection checks structural class metadata and qualifier meta-annotations without requiring annotation implementation Kotlin metadata to be at the compiler pin
Pinned 2.3.21 accepts the tested HIDDEN enum entry from another module; candidate conservatively rejects Kotlin semantic field annotations
No application build or performance claim

features.name: Generic Java instance-field reads through receiver substitution
features.scope: Specialize public generic Java instance-field signatures through receiver types and inherited generic supertypes while retaining the erased JVM descriptor and checked read boundaries.
restrictions: Public generic Java instance field signatures retain declaring-class type parameters, nullable/non-null declaration or root type-use annotations and erased JVM descriptors. Receiver substitution includes inherited generic supertypes, direct out/in/star reads, invariant nested lists/arrays and boxed primitives.

Generic writes and static generic field reads remain explicitly unsupported. Nested parameter-dependent reads through projected receivers, unrecognized field annotations, and non-null field enhancement of nullable source type parameters remain explicit boundaries. This is a bounded JVM language feature; no new unchanged app-file, Android execution, full-app compatibility or speed claim is made.

One fixed Java caller compiled against official Kotlin output runs against both providers under -Xverify:all, with independent value/null/exception/evaluation-count assertions. Public JVM signatures are compared. Original Sync.Entity<C>.content is relevance evidence; its application classpath is not substituted by the focused Java fixture.

features.name: Parameterized reference properties in data classes
features.scope: Validated parameterized JVM reference properties in otherwise-supported nongeneric data classes: Set, Map with nullable values, ordinary generic references, and nullable parameterized properties. Public constructors/getters/components/copy signatures, shallow copy/defaults, equality, hashCode, toString, null checks, and Kotlin metadata consumers are checked.
restrictions: Existing declaration/mutability restrictions, generic data-class declarations and array/function property restrictions remain.
Private backing-field generic signatures are not compared.
No unchanged app-file, Android build or performance claim in this independent differential report.

features.name: JvmField instance constructor and body properties
features.scope: JvmField instance constructor/body properties: public/protected and final/mutable JVM fields, absent generated accessors, field-only Kotlin metadata, initialization order, generic producer fields, source/library resolution and canonical annotation identity
restrictions: Static/object/companion and enum field lowering are outside this instance slice
JvmField value-class carrier properties, accessor annotations, volatile modifier combinations and declarations assigned later in init retain explicit unsupported boundaries
Generic field reading by Korrust retains existing independent interop bounds; generic field emission is checked through fixed Java/Kotlin consumers
No full Android module/application or performance claim

detail.resolution: The pinned compiler accepts and drops the explicit field annotation on a constructor parameter without val/var. Korrust rejects the nonexistent property backing-field target rather than adopting ignored annotation semantics.
detail.specification: references/kotlin-spec/docs/src/md/kotlin.core/annotations.md: allowed targets include a property backing field

features.name: Static JvmField properties in ordinary class companions and named objects
features.scope: Static JvmField on ordinary class companions and named objects: outer/object storage, initialization order, field-only metadata, absent generated accessors, source reads and writes, Java and Kotlin consumers, unchanged VersesUiModel
restrictions: Enum and interface companions, internal visibility, collisions with instance backing fields or singleton names retain explicit unsupported boundaries
Effectful object receiver expressions retain an explicit boundary; pinned compiler evaluation discrepancy is recorded separately
Existing value-class, volatile and accessor-annotation restrictions remain; no full Android module or performance claim
Compiled Kotlin static field consumption by Korrust is not claimed; independent official Kotlin consumers exercise emitted metadata
included_corrections: Companion getter bridge/helper emission correction belongs to this implementation and is not counted separately.

detail.resolution: Pinned compiler evaluates the assignment receiver but drops evaluation of the read receiver for static object fields. Korrust rejects nontrivial receivers explicitly rather than silently adopting receiver omission.

supporting_changes.name: Canonical nested classifier names in Kotlin metadata
Explicit getter diagnostic boundary
supporting_changes.note: The linked feature report precedes the diagnostic-only repair; final full-suite log supplies final-revision validation.

supporting_changes.name: Buffered classpath ZIP reads
supporting_changes.note: Retain the report-specific measurements and limits; no full-application speed claim.

supporting_changes.name: Wildcard imports before default classifiers
supporting_changes.scope: Explicit/renamed and same-package classifiers precede wildcard candidates; wildcard classes and supported typealiases precede platform/default imports. Repeated identical candidates deduplicate; conflicting candidates reject.

limitations: The nine sources with app dependencies require original sibling or Gradle-built artifacts; with just stdlib and JDK the official compiler also rejects these nine.

The unchanged-source survey measures compilation and class emission. Each runtime report identifies its own callers, provider revisions and coverage. A full AndroidBible build by Korrust was outside this survey.
